The wearer’s hands, tape measure, straightedge, sheet, and nearest stones are within the wearer’s arm’s reach, while the nearest stones are also within roughly 0.5–1 m of the second person’s feet. More gray blocks form a short curved or angled row along the upper part of the scene, approximately 0.7–1.5 m from the wearer, with rough soil or mortar behind them and a blue vertical object appearing near the upper-right in the fourth frame. Across the five frames, the viewpoint rotates and shifts rightward while remaining directed downward: the second person’s legs move from the left edge toward the upper-left/center and then become more peripheral, while the wearer’s knees and torso swing from center-right to center-left and back toward center.
